Let \(a=x,\ b=y,\ c=z,\ d=1-x-y-z\). Then \(T\) is the standard simplex in four barycentric coordinates, and

\[
I_n=\int_{a,b,c,d\ge 0,\ a+b+c+d=1} e^{-nabcd}\,da\,db\,dc.
\]

For \(\Re s>-1\), the Dirichlet integral gives

\[
\int_T (abcd)^s\,da\,db\,dc
=\frac{\Gamma(1+s)^4}{\Gamma(4+4s)}.
\]

Using Mellin inversion,

\[
e^{-nt}=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{\Re u=\alpha}\Gamma(u)n^{-u}t^{-u}\,du,
\qquad 0<\alpha<1,
\]

so

\[
I_n=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{\Re u=\alpha}
\Gamma(u)n^{-u}\frac{\Gamma(1-u)^4}{\Gamma(4-4u)}\,du.
\]

For large \(n\), shift the contour right past \(u=1\). The only contribution of order \(n^{-1}(\log n)^k\) comes from the pole at \(u=1\). Because the contour shift is to the right,

\[
I_n=-\operatorname*{Res}_{u=1}
\left[
\Gamma(u)n^{-u}\frac{\Gamma(1-u)^4}{\Gamma(4-4u)}
\right]+o(n^{-1}).
\]

Set \(v=u-1\) and \(L=\log n\). Then

\[
n^{-u}=n^{-1}e^{-Lv},
\]

and

\[
\Gamma(u)\frac{\Gamma(1-u)^4}{\Gamma(4-4u)}
=
\Gamma(1+v)\frac{\Gamma(-v)^4}{\Gamma(-4v)}.
\]

Using \(\Gamma(-v)=\Gamma(1-v)/(-v)\) and \(\Gamma(-4v)=\Gamma(1-4v)/(-4v)\),

\[
\Gamma(1+v)\frac{\Gamma(-v)^4}{\Gamma(-4v)}
=
-4v^{-3}B(v),
\]

where

\[
B(v)=\frac{\Gamma(1+v)\Gamma(1-v)^4}{\Gamma(1-4v)}.
\]

Now use

\[
\log\Gamma(1+w)=-\gamma w+\frac{\zeta(2)}2w^2+O(w^3).
\]

Thus

\[
\begin{aligned}
\log B(v)
&=\log\Gamma(1+v)+4\log\Gamma(1-v)-\log\Gamma(1-4v)\\
&=-\gamma v-\frac{11}{2}\zeta(2)v^2+O(v^3).
\end{aligned}
\]

Therefore

\[
B(v)=1-\gamma v+\frac{\gamma^2-11\zeta(2)}2v^2+O(v^3).
\]

The coefficient of \(v^{-1}\) in

\[
-4v^{-3}e^{-Lv}B(v)
\]

is

\[
-4\left(\frac{L^2}{2}+\gamma L+\frac{\gamma^2-11\zeta(2)}2\right).
\]

Because the residue enters with a minus sign,

\[
nI_n
=
2L^2+4\gamma L+2\gamma^2-22\zeta(2)+o(1).
\]

Since \(\zeta(2)=\pi^2/6\),

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\left(
nI_n-2(\log n)^2-4\gamma\log n
\right)
=
2\gamma^2-\frac{11\pi^2}{3}.
\]

\[
\boxed{2\gamma^2-\frac{11\pi^2}{3}}
\]
